hero.pill: HTTP and HTTPS monitoring with public status pages
hero.description: Uply checks your URLs on a schedule, measures their response time and opens an incident when a service goes down. Your team hears about it by email, Discord or Slack, and your users see it on a public status page.

notes.intervals: Checks from every 30 seconds to every hour
notes.channels: Alerts at the outage and at the recovery

showcase.title: Dashboard
showcase.caption: Sample data. Every card above is a real component of Uply.

features.description: Uply does a few things and does them on time: it checks, it confirms, it alerts and it keeps the history.

checks.title: Checks that confirm before they alert.
checks.text: Each monitor runs on its own interval, from every 30 seconds to every hour. A failed check runs again 20 seconds later, and a state only changes after two results in a row.

status_pages.title: A status page your users can read.
status_pages.text: Pick the monitors to show, name them your way and publish. The page shows 90 days of uptime and the recent incidents, never a URL or an error message.

alerts.title: Alerts where your team is
alerts.text: Email, Discord and Slack, when a service goes down and when it comes back up.

incidents.title: Incidents with a timeline
incidents.text: Opened at the first failure of a confirmed outage, resolved at the first success, with every alert sent.

dashboard.title: A live dashboard
dashboard.text: Uptime over 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days, response times and states, updated as the checks land.

timings.title: Where the time goes
timings.text: DNS, connect, TLS and first byte for each monitor, next to its recent checks.

teams.title: Built for teams
teams.text: Organizations, invitations by email and four roles: owner, admin, member and viewer.

security.title: A careful sign in
security.text: A verified email for every account, and two factor authentication with recovery codes.

capabilities.label: What Uply covers
capabilities.uptime: Uptime over 24 h, 7 d and 30 d
